case: candidate trial-0db61e9938-param-4be0257f failed its own installation self-check (internally caught AssertionErrors); the outer evaluation returned valid on the parent-fallback path. This plan acquires the missing evidence; it does not repair, accept or score the candidate. This revision repairs exactly one collector-interface defect in the previous generated probe (inputs/previous-diagnostic.py, sha256 8ab9078e..., the exact generated-before state audited in inputs/execution-failure.json): the per-window comparison-record cap was exhausted by PASSING self-check comparisons, so a later REAL failing comparison lost its operands and outcome. The repair is confined to evidence retention inside the install-window comparator observer; the original computation, once-only invocation, internally caught fallback behavior, quality thresholds, restoration and result/exception propagation are unchanged.
evidence_gap: Two layers. (1) Model-evidence gap (unchanged from the previous plan): the supplied records prove WHERE the candidate's setup self-checks aborted, but not WHAT the failing comparisons actually compared. Original observations: (a) inputs/failure.json (run-only CandidateTrace) records two internally caught AssertionErrors from torch.testing.assert_close during candidate installation - 'fused' mode at _check_logits with message 'decode logits mismatch (fused_eager_vs_parent_step_1)' (candidate line 537 caller, line 468 assertion) and 'exact' mode with 'decode logits mismatch (exact_chain_E_absorb)' (line 629 caller); the trace policy states these are locations, not causes; (b) the original candidate worker result (run/rank-0.json, indexed in inputs/evidence-index.json) shows valid=true, both continuous quality checks passed with max_abs_error 0.0, coverage counts 2x prefill passthrough and 62x decode 'parent_fallback_setup_failure', so the fast decode path never executed and the measured quality is the parent computation behind the replacement wrappers. Unknown: the operands and input/state provenance of each failing comparison were never captured - magnitudes and index distribution of the mismatches, whether they also violate the task acceptance tolerance 0.02/0.02 (the self-check uses a tighter 0.012/0.012, _VERIFY_ATOL/_VERIFY_RTOL), whether operand argmax tokens agree (the step-1 token gate at candidate line 535 passed before the failing line-537 assertion), and whether the two chain-E operands were produced at comparable decode positions (both calls receive the same cache object after the first call has already extended it). (2) Collector-interface gap (the defect repaired here, demonstrated on CPU by inputs/execution-failure.json): a full exact-mode setup performs ~197 assert_close calls (31 eager steps + 72 KV-layer finals + 31+31+31 chain checks + 1 chain E per candidate.py:511-630), all passing until the chain-E comparison aborts the mode; the previous observer admitted only the first _MAX_ASSERT_SITES=128 records and dropped every later call regardless of outcome (previous-diagnostic.py:_record_assert_entry lines 312-316), so the recorded failure would again have no operands, no comparison statistics and no outcome - 128 saved successes, failure_operands_or_outcome_saved=false in the audit. Without the repair, evidence gap (1) is unacquirable for exactly the failing comparisons that matter. With the repair, gap (1) becomes acquirable but is still not answered by generation: the leased-worker re-run must produce the observations.

source_mappings.meaning: Every comparator call now gets a cheap provenance entry (caller site from the Python stack, candidate-file stack frames, atol/rtol/equal_nan/msg kwargs, shape/dtype/device-level operand metadata; no tensor copies, no device synchronization) BEFORE the real comparator runs. After the real outcome is known: a passing call keeps full detail only while fewer than 128 records are retained (FIFO); a RAISING call is always retained up to 32 retained failures - if the 128-record list is full, the oldest retained passing record is evicted and leaves a provenance stub (seq, site, msg, evicted_for_failure_seq). Full detail (operand descriptions, float32 comparison statistics vs call and request tolerances, top<=64 violations, argmax agreement) is computed only for records that will be retained; for a raising call it is computed after the exception was raised, reading the still-live operands read-only. Every dropped or overflowed call is counted per site (assert_close_unretained_sites), with truthful totals (assert_close_total/passed/failed/unfinished, assert_close_overflow, assert_close_failure_overflow, evicted_success_records, evicted_stub_overflow). Retention is decided by the comparator's actual outcome, never by exception type routing or message text; all resource bounds are kept.

observations.kind: proposed measurement (install-window assert_close capture, repaired retention)
observations.statement: For every torch.testing.assert_close call made while a candidate bundle is being installed: the caller site (file/line/function from the stack, not from the message), the candidate-file stack frames, the call's atol/rtol/equal_nan/msg kwargs, bounded operand descriptions (shape/dtype/device/numel/finiteness/min/max), float32 comparison statistics (max/mean abs error, nonfinite count, counts of elements violating the call tolerance and the request acceptance tolerance), top<=64 violating elements (flat index, both values, abs error, allowed bound) and, for <=2-D floating operands, flat argmax/top-2 values and margin of each operand plus an argmax-agreement flag; plus, at window level, the truthful retention ledger (total/passed/failed/unfinished, retained failure count, evictions with provenance stubs, per-site unretained counts, caps).
observations.resolves: Whether the fused step-1 mismatch exceeds only the candidate's 0.012 self-check or also the 0.02/0.02 acceptance tolerance; its magnitude spectrum and index distribution; whether compared operands agree on the greedy token; whether chain-E operands look like same-position small drift or different-position gross divergence. The repair guarantees the failing chain-E comparison (call ~197, after ~196 successes) is captured with full operands and outcome instead of being dropped by the cap. These are observations of comparison operands, not causal conclusions.
observations.method: Time-scoped replacement of the torch.testing.assert_close module attribute inside the subclassed install(); the original function is always called afterwards with identical arguments and its exception object is re-raised unchanged after the outcome-driven retention step. Retention is decided by outcome (raised vs returned), never by message text or exception-type routing.
observations.bounds: <=128 detailed records per install window (FIFO for passing calls; raising calls guaranteed admission by evicting the oldest retained passing record); <=32 retained failing records per window (further failures counted per site, not stored); <=256 eviction stubs (further evictions counted); <=64 distinct unretained-site keys plus an 'other' bucket; <=64 top violations per site; transient CPU float32 copies of at most two operands per RETAINED site only (~0.6 MB for (1,151936) logits), released immediately; the cheap per-call entry performs no tensor copies and no synchronization; no tensors retained in evidence.
observations.error_behavior: Observer failures are recorded in instrumentation.errors and on the record (observer_error) and never mask, replace or suppress the original assert_close outcome; a comparator call terminated by BaseException (not Exception) is counted as unfinished and re-raised without retention.

observations.statement: For every candidate-internal call through context['references'] during the install window: sequence number, live spec identity (kind/target/phase read from the binding's specs), input_ids shape/dtype/device plus <=8 head and <=8 tail token ids, the past_key_values object identity token (id()), its get_seq_length() and layer count before the call, the result's logits shape/dtype, the returned cache's identity token and seq length, whether the returned cache IS the input cache object, and any raised exception type/message.
observations.resolves: Comparability of the compared executions: exact decode positions and cache aliasing for every oracle-chain and chain-E call; direct empirical test of the in-place-advance hypothesis (same object_id seen at consecutive calls with seq_length incremented between the ref_out and my_out calls); which token each side of every comparison actually consumed.
observations.method: Reference observers installed by swapping BindingSession.references only during super().install(); they call through to the captured original forward unchanged.
observations.bounds: <=2048 records per install window, FIFO cap unchanged from the previous probe (a full two-mode setup makes ~350 parent calls, ~6x headroom); each record <~500 bytes; object ids are process-scoped identity tokens usable only for within-run correlation.
observations.error_behavior: Errors from the wrapped parent call are recorded on the record and re-raised unchanged; after the window closes the observer is a pure passthrough.

perturbations: Install window only (candidate setup): each RETAINED comparison record adds two synchronous device-to-host float32 copies plus reduction/item() calls; the repaired observer additionally builds a small provenance dict for every call (no copies, no synchronization) and, for raising calls only, computes detail after the exception was raised while the operands are still referenced by the observer frame (read-only detach/cpu/float32; the exception object, traceback chain and operands are untouched). This lengthens result.setup.elapsed_ms, which the evaluator itself labels 'installation after model prepare; separate from the declared warm-model score' (evaluation.py:192). Warmup, repetitions, quality checks and their timings are untouched.

Post-install dormant observers: the binding's reference closures captured during install keep one extra no-op Python frame per parent-reference invocation on the fallback path during the measured runs (~32 calls per invocation; order 1e-5 relative to end_to_end_ms). Diagnostic timings are never acceptance scores; the original metrics fields are still produced by the unmodified evaluator.

Class-attribute swap: kernel_optimizer.project.binding.BindingSession is replaced by a behavior-delegating subclass for the duration of the original entry call and restored in a finally block; the evaluator's function-level import resolves the patched attribute only for bundle installs it actually performs (zero effect when bundles=[], as in the baseline arm). If the patch cannot be applied, the collector degrades to an uninstrumented original run and records instrumentation status 'failed' with observations absent.

Allocation/lifetime: transient CPU host copies bounded by ~2x operand size per retained site (<=~2.5 MB), freed immediately; eviction drops already-computed success detail to keep the evidence file bounded (wasted copy cost already spent, no extra allocation); no CUDA allocations, no cached-block or allocator-state changes, no tensors or model weights retained by the evidence; no gc calls, no empty_cache, no seed/TF32/dtype/precision changes; nothing written outside context['output'], so the worker's source-manifest assertions and revision checks are unaffected.

Synchronization: the collector itself adds no torch.cuda.synchronize beyond the implicit ones from .item()/.cpu() inside the install window; the evaluator's own synchronize boundaries and completion semantics are unchanged. The repair changes only which install-window records are kept, not when or how anything synchronizes.
limitations: Single diagnostic re-run per arm on one leased GPU; no cross-device or repeat-run statistics are collected, and run-to-run nondeterminism is not characterized here.

Observations exist only at sites the original control flow reaches: the fused mode aborts at its first failing step (step 1), so later fused steps are unobserved unless a rerun reaches them; the collector never continues past an exception the candidate itself treats as fatal to its setup.

Retention bounds that remain after the repair: passing comparisons keep full detail only for the first <=128 retained records (later ones appear only as per-site counts with no operand statistics); more than 32 failing comparisons per window are counted but not stored; eviction stubs are capped at 256 (further evictions counted only); the fused step-1 failure and chain-E failure of this case (1 per mode) are far inside these bounds.

The reference-call observer (O2) retains its original fixed FIFO cap of 2048 records with no failure-priority eviction; a reference call raising after 2048 recorded calls would lose its record the same way the comparator previously did. Expected headroom is ~6x (a full two-mode setup makes ~350 parent calls), so this was left unchanged to keep the repair narrow; it is a remaining defect class, documented rather than fixed.

Only Python-level calls through context['references'] and torch.testing.assert_close are observed; native kernels (Triton, cuBLAS/SDPA), other threads and non-reference aliases of the parent forward are invisible, mirroring the CandidateTrace's own stated scope.
object_id values are process-scoped identity tokens for within-run aliasing checks only; they are not stable across runs or files.

Operand statistics are computed from CPU float32 copies; bf16->float32 conversion is exact, but mean_abs_error accumulates in float32 and the copies are taken after any GPU-side nondeterminism has already occurred - the collector measures operands, not execution. Detail for a raising call is computed post-raise from the still-live operands; the values are the compared values, but the copy happens after the comparator's own internal error formatting already read them.

Nonfinite evidence is serialized as the string markers 'NaN'/'Infinity'/'-Infinity' because strict JSON (allow_nan=False, matching the framework's write_json) cannot carry them; absence is reported as null/absent fields, never fabricated; a dropped record is reported as dropped, never reconstructed.

The CPU checks run in this author session (compile, unit, retention-boundary and BindingSession-level integration tests with synthetic tensors, a fake adapter and a tiny module) validate mechanics only, including the exact audit scenario from inputs/execution-failure.json; they do not establish full-model or GPU behavior, and no GPU work was performed here. CPU mocks are not model quality.

A successful diagnostic re-run that returns valid=True with max_abs_error 0.0 establishes only that the parent-fallback path reproduced the reference within tolerance; it says nothing about the quality of the candidate's fused/exact interiors, which never execute.
No independent_reference tensors are supplied in this case, so no cross-source logits comparison is possible; that evidence is recorded as absent.
This collector produces no acceptance pair, no score and no repair; timings inside the diagnostic result must not be compared against baseline timings for acceptance.

Site identification uses caller file/line from the Python stack (code-derived instrumentation); it is deliberately not routed by error message text, and the msg kwarg is recorded verbatim only as data. The eviction policy (oldest retained passing record first) is positional, not informativeness-ranked.
unresolved: H1 (conditional hypothesis, decided by O1+O2): the chain-E comparison is ill-posed because the first _parent_decode already advanced the shared DynamicCache in place, so my_out decodes the same token one position later; prediction - same object_id at consecutive reference calls with seq_length 259 vs 258 at the two calls, operand argmax tokens differing and max_abs_error far beyond 0.02. If instead seq lengths match and the error is small, the hypothesis is wrong and the exact-mode absorb path needs different evidence. The repair makes this comparison's operands actually observable (previously lost to the cap); generation is not validation.

The alternative (gross divergence with many acceptance violations) would indicate a real defect in the Triton interior.

Whether the fused interior would fail at later steps, and whether the exact interior's all-steps pass would persist on other inputs - unobservable without modifying the candidate's control flow, which this collector does not do.
Root cause inside the fused Triton kernels (which kernel or op diverges) - would require the framework's operator-level profiling actions; out of scope for this collector.
Whether the candidate could ever be quality-valid with its fast path enabled - untested and untestable here, since enabling it would require changing the candidate.

Any statement about the recorded timings (candidate 736.77 ms vs baseline 701.76 ms end_to_end_ms medians) - not addressable: those are original observations, timing is not an acceptance pair, and this collector adds no timing evidence.

interface.caller_contract: The executor supplies each original baseline/candidate ExecutionRequest with only entry/function/output/wait settings changed and parameters.diagnostic_context added; the worker imports this file with cwd set to the original materialized source (kernel_optimizer/runtime/worker.py:76-82).

parameters: request (identity fields and quality tolerances only)

behavior: Imports the original evaluator entry exactly once and calls it with the unchanged context; the original evaluator keeps ownership of steps, warmup, repeats, binding, reference, thresholds, precision policies, reset and completion boundaries.

Runs the original evaluator exactly once per worker; no silent rerun of failures, no suppression of assertions, no acceptance changes, no forced GC, no precision/backend alterations, no writes outside context['output'].

Instrumentation is scoped to each bundle installation window and restored in finally blocks even on error; on instrumentation failure it degrades to an uninstrumented original run with status recorded and observations absent.

The internally caught candidate self-check exceptions remain internally caught: the collector observes them at the assert_close call without converting them into worker failures, and never force-enables any path or reruns the model.

Preserves the original return: on success the evaluator's result passes through with only an added 'diagnostic' index field; on error the original exception is re-raised unchanged after the evidence file has been persisted (worker rank status remains 'failed' with the original traceback).

Repaired retention (only change vs inputs/previous-diagnostic.py): install-window comparator recording is two-phase with outcome-driven retention - every call gets cheap provenance; passing calls occupy the bounded 128-record list FIFO; raising calls are always retained (<=32) by evicting the oldest retained passing record, leaving a provenance stub; all drops, evictions and overflows are counted per site; no resource bound was removed; retention is never routed by message text or exception type; the comparator's return values and exception objects are passed through untouched.

outputs.contents: context/diagnostic_context echo, runtime versions, instrumentation status/errors/caps (incl. retention caps), identity (paths+sha256 for adapter, bundle files and specs, reference .pt, original entry, collector, optional independent_reference), install_windows per bundle: reference_calls (FIFO 2048) + assert_close_sites (<=128 detailed records incl. <=32 failures), retention_policy string, and the retention ledger (assert_close_total/passed/failed/unfinished, assert_close_overflow, assert_close_failure_overflow, assert_close_retained_failures, evicted_success_records, evicted_success_stubs <=256, evicted_stub_overflow, assert_close_unretained_sites <=64 keys + other), original_outcome (returned/error/traceback), limitations pointer
outputs.size_bound: target <~1.5 MB per rank; caps: 2048 reference calls, 128 detailed comparison records, 32 retained failures, 256 eviction stubs, 64 unretained-site keys, 64 top violations per site, 12 stack frames, 8 head/tail tokens per window; no tensors, weights, caches or multi-GB state are stored - raw values are limited to the bounded top-violation elements needed to support exact re-comparison
outputs.raw_value_policy: All values live in this one small JSON artifact under the worker output; the server stores nothing else, and the result's diagnostic field carries only its path/sha256.
